arxiv-2005-12307.title: Complex magnetic ordering and associated topological Hall effect in a two-dimensional metallic chiral magnet
arxiv-2005-12307.creator: Nyayabanta Swain, Munir Shahzad and Pinaki Sengupta
arxiv-2005-12307.description: Abstract Motivated by recent experiments on the observation of room temperature skyrmions in a layered heterostructure and subsequent demonstration of topological Hall effect in the same system, we have studied a minimal model of itinerant electrons coupled to local moments with competing interactions in an external magnetic field.

arxiv-2104-14266.title: Axiomatizations and Computability of Weighted Monadic Second-Order Logic PubID: pubid: 978-1-6654-4895-6/21/$31.00 ©2021 IEEE
arxiv-2104-14266.creator: Antonis Achilleos, Mathias Ruggaard Pedersen
arxiv-2104-14266.description: Abstract Weighted monadic second-order logic is a weighted extension of monadic second-order logic that captures exactly the behaviour of weighted automata. Its semantics is parameterized with respect to a semiring on which the values that weighted formulas output are evaluated.

arxiv-2109-14120.title: Meta Learning on a Sequence of Imbalanced Domains with Difficulty Awareness
arxiv-2109-14120.creator: Zhenyi Wang, Tiehang Duan, Le Fang, Qiuling Suo, Mingchen Gao
arxiv-2109-14120.description: Abstract Recognizing new objects by learning from a few labeled examples in an evolving environment is crucial to obtain excellent generalization ability for real-world machine learning systems. A typical setting across current meta learning algorithms assumes a stationary task distribution during meta training.

arxiv-2208-08145.title: Stereo Superpixel Segmentation Via Decoupled Dynamic Spatial-Embedding Fusion Network
arxiv-2208-08145.creator: Hua Li, Junyan Liang ∗ *, Ruiqi Wu, Runmin Cong, Wenhui Wu, Sam Tak Wu Kwong, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2208-08145.description: Abstract Stereo superpixel segmentation aims at grouping the discretizing pixels into perceptual regions through left and right views more collaboratively and efficiently. Existing superpixel segmentation algorithms mostly utilize color and spatial features as input, which may impose strong constraints on spatial information while utilizing the disparity information in terms of stereo image pairs.

arxiv-2307-07843.title: Transformers are Universal Predictors
arxiv-2307-07843.creator: Sourya Basu, Moulik Choraria, Lav R. Varshney
arxiv-2307-07843.description: Abstract We find limits to the Transformer architecture for language modeling and show it has a universal prediction property in an information-theoretic sense. We further analyze performance in non-asymptotic data regimes to understand the role of various components of the Transformer architecture, especially in the context of data-efficient training.

arxiv-2307-12434.title: Arndt and De Morgan Integer Compositions
arxiv-2307-12434.creator: Brian Hopkins, Aram Tangboonduangjit
arxiv-2307-12434.description: Abstract . In 2013, Joerg Arndt recorded that the Fibonacci numbers count integer compositions where the first part is greater than the second, the third part is greater than the fourth, etc. We provide a new combinatorial proof that verifies his observation using compositions with only odd parts as studied by De Morgan.

arxiv-2308-02379.title: Monodromy of the Radon transform M. Dettweiler: Department of Mathematics, University of Bayreuth, 95440 Bayreuth, Germany; michael.dettweiler@uni-bayreuth.de S. Reiter: Department of Mathematics, University of Bayreuth, 95440 Bayreuth, Germany; stefan.reiter@uni-bayreuth.de
arxiv-2308-02379.creator: Meirav Amram
arxiv-2308-02379.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Meirav Amram. We algorithmically determine the monodromy of the local system on the smooth part of the Radon transformation of a generic simple perverse sheaf on the projective plane. Introduction The classical Radon transform is an integral transformation which sends a suitably integrable function f on the projective plane {\mathbb{P}}^{2}(\mathbb{R}) to the function \mathcal{R}(f)\,:\,\widetilde{{\mathbb{P}}}^{2}(\mathbb{R})\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\mathbb{R},\,\,\,\widetilde{x}\mapsto\int_{L_{\widetilde{x}}}f\,, on the dual plane \widetilde{{\mathbb{P}}}^{2}(\mathbb{R}), where L_{\widetilde{x}}\subseteq{\mathbb{P}}^{2}(\mathbb{R}) is the line corresponding to an element \widetilde{x} in the dual plane [ 14 ] .

arxiv-2309-06943.title: Effect of hyperparameters on variable selection in random forests
arxiv-2309-06943.creator: Cesaire J. K. Fouodo, Lea L. Kronziel, Inke R. König, Silke Szymczak
arxiv-2309-06943.description: Abstract Random forests (RFs) are well suited for prediction modeling and variable selection in high-dimensional omics studies. The effect of hyperparameters of the RF algorithm on prediction performance and variable importance estimation have previously been investigated. However, how hyperparameters impact RF-based variable selection remains unclear.

arxiv-2310-08864.title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
arxiv-2310-08864.creator: O pen X - E mbodiment Collaboration robotics-transformer-x.github.io, Abby O’Neill, Abdul Rehman, Abhinav Gupta, Abhiram Maddukuri, Abhishek Gupta, Abhishek Padalkar, Abraham Lee, Acorn Pooley, Agrim Gupta, Ajay Mandlekar, Ajinkya Jain, Albert Tung, Alex Bewley, Alex Herzog, Alex Irpan, Alexander Kh
arxiv-2310-08864.description: Abstract Large, high-capacity models trained on diverse datasets have shown remarkable successes on efficiently tackling downstream applications. In domains from NLP to Computer Vision, this has led to a consolidation of pretrained models, with general pretrained backbones serving as a starting point for many applications. Can such a consolidation happen in robotics?

arxiv-2402-14980.title: Comparative Analysis of Data Preprocessing Methods, Feature Selection Techniques and Machine Learning Models for Improved Classification and Regression Performance on Imbalanced Genetic Data
arxiv-2402-14980.creator: Arshmeet Kaur, Morteza Sarmadi
arxiv-2402-14980.description: Abstract Rapid advancements in genome sequencing have led to the collection of vast amounts of genomics data. Researchers may be interested in using machine learning models on such data to predict the pathogenicity or clinical significance of a genetic mutation.

arxiv-2405-18507.title: Injecting Hierarchical Biological Priors into Graph Neural Networks for Flow Cytometry Prediction
arxiv-2405-18507.creator: Fatemeh Nassajian Mojarrad, Lorenzo Bini, Thomas Matthes, Stéphane Marchand-Maillet
arxiv-2405-18507.description: Abstract In the complex landscape of hematologic samples such as peripheral blood or bone marrow derived from flow cytometry (FC) data, cell-level prediction presents profound challenges. This work explores injecting hierarchical prior knowledge into graph neural networks (GNNs) for single-cell multi-class classification of tabular cellular data.

arxiv-2409-09848.title: A Comprehensive Survey of PID and Pure Pursuit Control Algorithms for Autonomous Vehicle Navigation
arxiv-2409-09848.creator: Harshit Jain ∗, Priyal Babel ∗
arxiv-2409-09848.description: Abstract The autonomous driving industry is experiencing unprecedented growth, driven by rapid advancements in technology and increasing demand for safer, more efficient transportation. At the heart of this revolution are two critical factors: lateral and longitudinal controls, which together enable vehicles to track complex environments with high accuracy and minimal errors.

arxiv-2409-12329.title: Analysis of high-field side plasma instabilities in tokamak edge Journal: Journal of Nuclear Materials and Energy
arxiv-2409-12329.creator: M.V. Umansky
arxiv-2409-12329.description: Abstract Balanced double-null configurations are of general interest for boundary plasma physics, and they have been proposed for some future designs. Experimental observations demonstrate absence of plasma fluctuations in tokamak high-field side scrape-off layer in a balanced double-null configuration [Smick et al 2013 Nucl.

Log anomaly detection (LogAD) is crucial for identifying failures and threats in large-scale computing and cyberinfrastructure systems.

arxiv-2509-11772.title: Seg2Track-SAM2: SAM2-based Multi-object Tracking and Segmentation for Zero-shot Generalization
arxiv-2509-11772.creator: D. Mendonça, T. Barros, C. Premebida, U.J. Nunes
arxiv-2509-11772.description: Abstract Autonomous systems require robust Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) capabilities to operate reliably in dynamic environments. MOT ensures consistent object identity assignment and precise spatial delineation. Recent advances in foundation models, such as SAM2, have demonstrated strong zero-shot generalization for video segmentation, but their direct application to MOTS (MOT+Segmentation) remains limited by insufficient identity management and memory efficiency.

arxiv-2510-07940.title: TTOM: Test-Time Optimization and Memorization for Compositional Video Generation
arxiv-2510-07940.creator: Leigang Qu, Ziyang Wang, Na Zheng, Wenjie Wang, Liqiang Nie, Tat-Seng Chua
arxiv-2510-07940.description: Abstract Video Foundation Models (VFMs) exhibit remarkable visual generation performance, but struggle in compositional scenarios ( e.g. , motion, numeracy, and spatial relation). In this work, we introduce Test-Time Optimization and Memorization (TTOM) , a training-free framework that aligns VFM outputs with spatiotemporal layouts during inference for better text-image alignment.

pmc-11713240.title: Sex Differences in the Clinical Manifestation of AD Pathology in Early‐Stage Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11713240.creator: Erin E. Sundermann, Sarah Banks, Mark W. Bondi, Maricedes Acosta Martinez, Anat Biegon, Lindsay J Rotblatt, Thomas Hildebrandt
pmc-11713240.description: BackgroundDespite women showing greater pathological tau burden than men in the preclinical and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) stages of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), they show a cognitive advantage, particularly in verbal memory, followed by a steeper decline. Thus, the question of sex differences in the clinical manifestation of AD pathology is important, but underexamined.

pmc-13266726.title: Development and internal validation of a CT radiomics-based model for severity classification in HIV-associated Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
pmc-13266726.creator: Yu Wang, Wei Wang, Caopei Zheng, Yuqing Sun, Budong Chen, Yulin Zhang
pmc-13266726.description: BackgroundSeverity assessment of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-associated Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) is clinically important because arterial blood gas indices are standard but may not fully capture the heterogeneity of lung involvement on chest computed tomography (CT). We aimed to develop and internally validate a CT radiomics model for classifying severity in adults with confirmed HIV-associated PJP.

uslaw-usc-t42-s15702.title: 42 U.S.C. § 15702 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t42-s15702.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s15702.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 148 (Windstorm Impact Reduction). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In this chapter: (1) Director The term “Director” means the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2) Lifelines The term “lifelines” means public works and utilities, including transportation facilities and infrastructure, oil and gas pipelines, electrical power and communication.
